svg.title: ECS building blocks - image, task definition, service, task, container, target group
svg.text: From image to traffic — how the ECS pieces fit together
Worked example: the Strobe agent. Numbers follow the order things happen. Task #2 shows what changes if the desired count were 2.
together; does nothing on its own
A recipe: says what a task looks like.
Every edit creates a new revision.
A manager: keeps N tasks alive,
replaces dead ones, rolls out new
A list the ALB reads: which IP:port
addresses may get traffic right now,
and how to test they are alive.
I never edit this list by hand —
registers each new task’s IP:3000 · removes it when the task stops
The task definition names which image to run (plus CPU, memory, port, env, health check).
The ECS service is told which task definition revision to run and how many copies (desired count).
The service launches tasks: Fargate pulls the image, starts the container, gives the task its own IP.
The service registers each task’s IP:port in the target group, and removes it when the task stops.
The target group health-checks every target (GET /healthz); only passing targets get traffic.
The ALB rule /acp* forwards to the target group, which hands the request to a healthy task.
My code + runtime, packaged and stored in ECR
Blueprint for a task: image(s), CPU/memory, port, env, health check
One running copy of a task definition; on Fargate it has its own IP
The program running inside a task, started from an image
Keeps N tasks running, replaces failures, rolls out revisions, syncs TG
The ALB’s list of task IP:port targets + how to health-check them
Logical home for services and tasks (Fargate: no servers to manage)
